newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, Oct 30 - Luanda, Lobito, Namibe - Working normally, with no delays reported. Soyo, Kwanda base - Base currently receiving cargoes alongside jetty. Oil service base still being rebuilt. Crude oil terminals loading according to schedule. Cabinda - SBM3 - Deepwater loading ports expected to be back in service 15 November.

ISRAEL, Nov 5 - Haifa - Five vessels due, 1-2 days delay. Loading/discharging at berth 4 general cargo, 1 bulk, 4 containers, 2 tankers, 1 passenger, no vessels discharging at anchorage. Vessels waiting at anchorage to load/discharge 1 general cargo, 1 bulk with 2 days delay, 3 containers, 1 bunkering, 4 under repair/dry-dock, 4 awaiting orders. Ashdod - One to two days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth 6 general cargo, 1 bulk, 1 container, 1 car carrier, 1 tanker, 1 passenger. No vessels discharging at anchorage. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge 1 bulk, 1 container. Eilat - Loading/discharging at berth 1 bulk, 1 container, 1 passenger.
LIBERIA, Oct 31 - Monrovia - Curfew has been extended and is now in force from 1900 hrs to 0600 hrs. This is expected to cause some disruption to port operations.

MOZAMBIQUE, Nov 4 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing at night. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally. Container terminal/other terminals working normally. Pilotage now possible 24 hours per day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugs fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maputo - Pilotage now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 120 metres loa with maximum draft of 9 metres. Two tugs (one out of order). Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangement with port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so (first come-first served basis). Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres plus the rise of tide.
NAMIBIA, Nov 4 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.
NIGERIA, Oct 31 - Lagos - Port working normally. No berthing delays at any terminal. Port Harcourt - Quiet. No delays reported. All crude terminals loading according to schedule.

SOUTH AFRICA, Nov 4 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths fully committed with berthing delays of between 24-48 hours at present. Bulk import berths fully committed. Berth 701 should be working normally from 6/11, but berth 702 is still experiencing lengthy delays. Bulk export berths (minerals working normally. Bulk cl berths vessels berthing on arrival at present. However, 8 vessels are arriving on 5/11 and 6/11 and berthing delays of approx. 12-24 can be expected. Durban - Container terminal delays of up to 48 hours being experienced at present. Point/New pier/Maydon wharf berths working normally for general cargo vessels, but delays to wheat dischargers can be expected.

Maize terminal (Maydon wharf 8) - One maize loader and 1 sunflower loader for November. Citrus terminal - Season ended 1/11. Bunk supplies fluid - Delays of up to 6 hours in supplying bunkers can be expected due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock fully booked for November. East london - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Extremely busy but no delays. Dry-dock fully booked up to 15/12, thereafter open for bookings. Copper moving in small parcels of 2,500 tonnes per month in containers to the Far East. Elevator - 1 Vessel due mid-November, thereafter no exports unless the pace increase of $20,000 imposed by the maize board is dropped. Gas oil pipeline under utilised. Scrap steel 8,500 tonnes on hand ready for shipment. Tankers expected to be busy until end December.

Port Elizabeth - Working normally with 2 vessels in port. No delays expected. Citrus season completed and the next ore vessel is due mid-November. Container berth no delays expected unless vessels eta clash or strong winds cause disruption. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths no delays, with vessels working on arrival. Container terminal - No delays expected for the coming week. Bunker berths Duncan dock will be out of commission for IFO supplies from 4-15/11. Dry-docks, repair quay fully occupied, booking essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Nov 2 - Sfax - Three vessels in port operating, all discharging, of which 1 bagged sugar, 1 general cargo, 1 bulk sulphur. Sousse - Three in port of which 1 discharging marble chips, 2 military, no waiting time, no vessels awaiting orders. Tunis - Two vessels in port of which 1 awaiting instructions, 1 general cargo vessel. Rades - Four vessels in port of which 1 discharging bananas, 3 ro/ros. La Goulette - North side - 1 General cargo vessel, 1 passenger, 1 military, 1 discharging maize. South side - 1 Discharging grain, 3 in roads. Nov 4 - Bizerte - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Two vessels in port, discharging, of which 1 sugar, 1 steel. Zarzis - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. No vessels in port.

YEMEN, Nov 3 - Hodeidah - Three berths occupied, all others vacant. Three vessels berthed of which 1 flour, 1 steel, 1 general cargo, 1 anchored, waiting to load. Berthing delays general cargo up to 2 days, bagged up to 4 days, bulk up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - Both berths occupied (1 general cargo vessel, 1 flour vessel). No vessels anchored, 2 days berthing delay expected.
